vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_USE_AFTER_FREE_DANGLING_POINTER_NOT_NULLIFIED

root_cause.description: remove_animal frees the animal struct (and its name buffer) but does NOT set the zoo[idx] pointer to NULL afterward. The dangling pointer remains in the zoo pointer array. report_name's only safety check is zoo[idx] != NULL, which passes on the freed slot because the pointer was never cleared. This allows report_name to dereference freed memory: it loads a function pointer from struct+0x00 and a name pointer from struct+0x10, then performs an indirect call (call rdx). If the freed struct memory is reused by a subsequent allocation of matching size (e.g., a name buffer of 24 bytes via add_animal with name_length=24), the attacker controls the content of the reused memory through read(), thereby controlling both the function pointer (struct+0x00) and the name pointer (struct+0x10) that report_name dereferences.

affected_objects: zoo global pointer array at 0x4040c8 (10 slots, indices 0-9)
animal struct (24 bytes / malloc(0x18)): offset 0x00 = function pointer, offset 0x08 = type, offset 0x10 = name buffer pointer
name buffer (user-controlled size 0-63 bytes via malloc(name_length))

data_flow: Attacker calls add_animal (menu option 1): allocates 24-byte animal struct via malloc(0x18), sets struct[0x00]=speak(0x4012cd), struct[0x08]=type, allocates name buffer via malloc(name_length), reads name_length bytes from stdin into name buffer, stores struct pointer in zoo[idx], increments count.

Attacker calls remove_animal (menu option 2) with the same zone index: frees zoo[idx]->name (struct+0x10) at 0x40175c, then frees zoo[idx] (the struct itself) at 0x40177c. zoo[idx] is NOT set to NULL. Count is decremented.

Attacker calls add_animal again with name_length=24 (0x18): malloc(24) may return the previously freed struct memory (glibc 2.39 tcache LIFO for 0x20-size-class allocations). The slot search in add_animal skips non-NULL slots, so the new struct goes to a different zoo slot, but the name buffer (malloc(24)) occupies the old struct's memory. Attacker writes 24 bytes of controlled data via read(0, buf, 24) into this name buffer, which overlaps the old struct location.

Attacker calls report_name (menu option 3) with the original freed zone index: zoo[idx] is still non-NULL (dangling pointer), so the NULL check passes. report_name loads rdx from struct+0x00 (attacker-controlled function pointer) and rdi from struct+0x10 (attacker-controlled name pointer), then executes 'call rdx' at 0x4018bf — indirect call to attacker-controlled address.

security_check.expected: After freeing an animal struct in remove_animal, the zoo[idx] pointer should be set to NULL to prevent subsequent access to freed memory. Additionally, report_name should validate that the struct is still live (not freed) before dereferencing its fields.
security_check.actual: remove_animal frees zoo[idx]->name and zoo[idx] but does NOT zero zoo[idx]. report_name only checks zoo[idx] != NULL (at 0x40186f-0x401872), which is insufficient because the dangling pointer is non-NULL. No use-after-free detection or double-allocation guard exists.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing NULL assignment after free in remove_animal (the pointer is left dangling). Missing lifetime validation in report_name (NULL check does not distinguish live vs freed pointers).

vulnerable_operation.operation: indirect call via function pointer loaded from freed/reused heap memory
vulnerable_operation.target: freed animal struct memory that may be reused by a name buffer allocation of size 24 (0x18), controlled by attacker via read()
vulnerable_operation.size: 8 bytes for function pointer (struct+0x00), 8 bytes for name pointer (struct+0x10)

impact.reason: After remove_animal frees the struct without NULLing zoo[idx], the dangling pointer allows report_name to access freed heap memory. If the freed memory is reused by a subsequent allocation of matching size (24 bytes), the struct fields (function pointer at +0x00, name pointer at +0x10) are overwritten with attacker-controlled data from read(). This constitutes memory corruption of the struct's semantic fields through a use-after-free.

The animal struct's function pointer (offset 0x00) and name pointer (offset 0x10) can be corrupted when freed struct memory is reused by a name buffer allocation. The attacker writes arbitrary data via read() into the name buffer, which overlaps the struct memory, corrupting the function pointer and name pointer fields.

If the freed struct memory is accessed by report_name without being reused (or reused with non-callable data), the indirect call 'call rdx' at 0x4018bf will dereference an invalid or uninitialized function pointer, causing a SIGSEGV crash.

evidence.description: remove_animal calls free(zoo[idx]->name) at 0x40175c (loading struct+0x10 into rdi, calling free@plt), then calls free(zoo[idx]) at 0x40177c (loading the struct pointer into rdi, calling free@plt). After both frees, the code proceeds to decrement the count at 0x40179a-0x4017a3. There is NO instruction between the free calls and the function epilogue that writes NULL/0 to zoo[8+idx*8]. The pointer remains dangling.

report_name loads zoo[8+idx*8] into rax at 0x40186b, tests rax at 0x40186f (test rax,rax), and jumps to proceed if non-NULL (jne 0x401885). Since the dangling pointer from remove_animal is non-NULL, this check passes. Then at 0x40189d it loads rdx = [rax] (function pointer from struct+0x00), at 0x4018b8 loads rax = [rax+0x10] (name pointer from struct+0x10), moves it to rdi at 0x4018bc, and executes 'call rdx' at 0x4018bf — an indirect call using a value loaded from potentially freed/reused memory.

add_animal allocates the name buffer via malloc(name_length) at 0x4015b8, where name_length is user-controlled in range [0,63] (checked at 0x40159c-0x4015aa: js or jg 0x3f rejected). It then calls read(0, name_buf, name_length) at 0x401602, writing user-controlled data into the buffer. If name_length=24 (0x18), this allocation matches the freed animal struct size (malloc(0x18) at 0x4014a8), enabling heap reuse of the freed struct memory.

add_animal's slot search iterates idx 0-9 checking if zoo[8+idx*8] == NULL (test rax,rax; je 0x4014a7 at 0x401499). Since remove_animal does NOT NULL the pointer, freed slots appear occupied. New animals are stored in different slots. This means the dangling pointer at the freed slot and the new struct pointer at a different slot can coexist, and if the new name buffer reuses the freed struct's heap memory, the dangling pointer accesses attacker-controlled data.

The complete UAF chain: (1) remove_animal frees the 24-byte struct without NULLing zoo[idx]; (2) add_animal with name_length=24 allocates a 24-byte name buffer that may reuse the freed struct memory (glibc 2.39 tcache LIFO for same-size-class allocations); (3) attacker writes 24 bytes of controlled data into the name buffer via read(), overwriting the struct's function pointer (offset 0x00) and name pointer (offset 0x10); (4) report_name dereferences the dangling zoo[idx] pointer, loads the attacker-controlled function pointer into rdx, and executes 'call rdx'.

verification_required: Dynamic verification that malloc(24) for a name buffer reuses the memory of a previously freed 24-byte animal struct under glibc 2.39 tcache behavior
Dynamic verification that the indirect call 'call rdx' at 0x4018bf executes with attacker-controlled rdx when the UAF chain is triggered

Verification of whether IBT (Indirect Branch Tracking) is enforced at runtime — if enforced, 'call rdx' to a non-ENDBR64 target would raise a #CP exception, potentially blocking control flow hijack (but the target get_shell at 0x401276 starts with endbr64, so it would pass IBT)

vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_USE_AFTER_FREE_INFO_LEAK_VIA_FREED_NAME_POINTER

root_cause.description: Same root cause as BUG-001: remove_animal does not NULL zoo[idx] after free, leaving a dangling pointer. When report_name accesses the freed struct, it loads the name pointer from struct+0x10 and passes it to print() which calls printf(': %s\n', name_ptr). If the freed struct memory has been partially reused or contains stale heap metadata, the name pointer field may point to arbitrary memory, and printf %s will read and print memory contents as a string until a null byte is encountered, causing an information leak.

affected_objects: animal struct name pointer field at offset 0x10
freed name buffer or reused heap memory

data_flow: Attacker calls add_animal to create an animal with a name buffer.
Attacker calls remove_animal to free the struct and name buffer without NULLing zoo[idx].

Attacker calls report_name on the freed slot: zoo[idx] is non-NULL (dangling), check passes. report_name loads struct+0x10 (name pointer) into rdi and calls the function pointer at struct+0x00. If the function pointer still resolves to speak/print (e.g., struct memory not yet reused), print() calls printf(': %s\n', name_ptr) where name_ptr points to freed memory. printf reads freed/reused heap memory as a string, potentially leaking heap contents.

security_check.expected: The name pointer should be validated as pointing to a live, valid allocation before being passed to printf as a %s argument.
security_check.actual: No validation of the name pointer's validity. The only check is zoo[idx] != NULL, which does not distinguish live from freed pointers.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing lifetime validation for the name buffer pointer. After free, the pointer in struct+0x10 becomes stale but is still dereferenced by printf %s.

vulnerable_operation.operation: printf('%s', freed_name_pointer) — reading freed heap memory as a string
vulnerable_operation.address: 0x4012c5 (inside print, called from speak called from report_name at 0x4018bf)
vulnerable_operation.target: freed name buffer or heap memory at the address stored in struct+0x10

impact.reason: If the freed struct's function pointer (offset 0x00) still contains the original speak address (0x4012cd) because the memory hasn't been reused yet, report_name will call speak→print→printf(': %s\n', name_ptr) where name_ptr (struct+0x10) points to the freed name buffer. The freed name buffer may contain stale heap metadata or data from reused allocations, which printf will read and print as a string, leaking heap memory contents.

If the freed name pointer (struct+0x10) points to memory that has been reclaimed and contains an invalid address, or if the struct memory itself has been reused such that struct+0x10 contains a non-mapped address, printf %s will dereference it and cause a SIGSEGV.

evidence.description: print() calls printf at 0x4012c5 with format string ': %s\n' (loaded from 0x40203f) and rsi = msg (the name pointer from struct+0x10). printf %s reads memory at the name pointer address until a null byte, with no length bound. If the name pointer is stale (pointing to freed memory), this reads freed heap contents.

report_name loads the name pointer from struct+0x10 at 0x4018b8 (mov rax, [rax+0x10]) and passes it as rdi to the indirect call at 0x4018bf. If the function pointer (struct+0x00) is still speak (0x4012cd), speak passes rdi to print, which passes it to printf %s. The name pointer from freed memory may point to freed/reused heap, causing an unbounded string read.

verification_required: Dynamic verification that the freed struct's function pointer field retains the original speak address long enough for the info-leak path to trigger before memory reuse
Dynamic verification that printf %s on the freed name pointer actually leaks non-trivial heap data (vs. crashing or printing empty string)

non_vulnerabilities.description: menu reads choice via scanf(%d) and validates 0 <= choice <= 4 using signed comparison (js at 0x4016f3 for negative, cmp eax,0x9; jle for upper bound in remove_animal/report_name context). The choice is used only for dispatch, not as an index.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: Bounds check is correct: negative values rejected by js, values > 4 rejected by jg. No index dereference based on menu choice. No vulnerability.

non_vulnerabilities.description: name_length is validated in range [0, 63] via js (negative rejected) and cmp eax,0x3f; jg (values > 63 rejected). The malloc(name_length) and read(0, buf, name_length) use the same variable for both size and read length, so no size mismatch.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The bounds check on name_length is correct and consistent. The same variable controls both malloc size and read length, preventing buffer overflow. The name_length=0 case (malloc(0)) returns a minimal allocation per glibc behavior, and read(0, buf, 0) reads 0 bytes — no overflow. The vulnerability is not in add_animal itself but in how its allocations interact with remove_animal's missing NULL assignment (BUG-001).

non_vulnerabilities.description: zone_index is validated in range [0, 9] via js (negative rejected) and cmp eax,0x9; jle (values > 9 rejected). The zoo[idx] != NULL check is present before freeing.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The index bounds check is correct — no OOB access on the zoo array. The vulnerability is not in the index validation but in the missing NULL assignment after free (BUG-001).

non_vulnerabilities.description: zone_index is validated in range [0, 9] via js and cmp eax,0x9; jle. The zoo[idx] != NULL check is present.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The index bounds check is correct — no OOB access. The vulnerability is that the NULL check is insufficient to prevent UAF (BUG-001/BUG-002), not that the index validation is wrong.

non_vulnerabilities.description: print calls system() with a hardcoded string ('/usr/bin/date +"%Y/%m/%d %H:%M.%S" | tr -d \'\n:\'') loaded from .rodata at 0x402010. The system() argument is not user-controlled.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The system() call uses a hardcoded command string from read-only .rodata. No command injection via the system() argument. The printf %s with the msg argument is only dangerous when msg comes from freed memory (BUG-002), not when called with a valid live name pointer.

non_vulnerabilities.description: init calls setvbuf to disable buffering on stdin/stdout/stderr and alarm(60) to set a timeout.
non_vulnerabilities.reason: No vulnerability. Standard initialization. The alarm(60) may limit exploitation time but is not itself a vulnerability.

unresolved.description: Whether glibc 2.39 tcache will reuse the freed 24-byte animal struct memory for a subsequent malloc(24) name buffer allocation
unresolved.reason: Static analysis confirms the sizes match (both malloc(0x18)=24 bytes, which falls in the 0x20 tcache bin). However, actual reuse depends on tcache state, allocation order, and whether other allocations intervene. Dynamic verification is needed to confirm the heap reuse.

unresolved.description: Whether IBT (Indirect Branch Tracking) is enforced at runtime, which would block 'call rdx' to addresses not starting with endbr64
unresolved.reason: The ELF marks IBT as enabled (GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_IBT), but actual enforcement depends on kernel support and CPU CET features.
